# Scaffold verification report

Verification of the zero-core workspace scaffold on 2026-09-30, run on the
Windows 11 host with cargo 1.96 and the `zero-core-lint` Docker image (rust
stable 1.98.1 with rustfmt and clippy). Nothing was committed; the tree is
untracked and waits for the owner's first commit.

## Files changed by the verifier

- `bindings/node/build.rs`: crate doc comment (the audited table denies `missing_docs`).
- `bindings/node/src/lib.rs`: `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on `version()` with the existing `// SAFETY:` block, following the zero-ffi convention.
- `bindings/python/packages/native/src/lib.rs`: the same per-item allow on `version()`.
- `docs/about/releasing.md`: new, adapted from pamoja's page with the 0.1.0 version and zero-server names; a `PROSE_SITES` entry of version.rs.
- `bindings/node/packages/sdk/package.json` and `bindings/node/package-lock.json`: `@zero-server/sdk` from 2.0.0-alpha.0 to 0.1.0 so every package shares the workspace version.
- `README.md`: names the workspace version 0.1.0 and says `@zero-server/sdk` 2.0 instead of 2.0.0 (version.rs treats every bare x.y.z in the README as the workspace version).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `## [Unreleased]` became `## [0.1.0] - Unreleased` so `version --check` finds the entry; the date is filled at the tag.
- `crates/xtask/src/site/mod.rs`: ten site integration tests marked `#[ignore = "needs the docs pages and the web tree, which are not written yet"]`; the goals table assertion.
- `crates/xtask/src/site/home.rs`: `the_map_puts_each_engine_crate_where_it_belongs` ignored the same way; `milestone` renamed to `goal`.
- `scripts/lint-wording.mjs`: `aria-labelledby` added to ALLOWED.

## Deviations from R.1

Gathered from the agents that built the scaffold, plus the verifier's own.

### Verifier

- Eleven xtask tests that load the repository tree (`site::tests::*` and `site::home::tests::the_map_puts_each_engine_crate_where_it_belongs`) are ignored with a reason rather than deleted or left red: they need docs/*.md pages, web/site.css, web/home.css, web/reference.css, web/js/{site,home,consoles,reference}.js and web/home.toml in pamoja's shape, none of which R.1 produces. Several still assert pamoja names (`docs/guides/modbus.html`, `zero_mqtt`, `zero-dashboard`) and must be reshaped when the site is built.
- `@zero-server/sdk` in the tree is 0.1.0 (private, unpublished) rather than 2.0.0-alpha.0: the design's one-version rule and `xtask version` require it. The published SDK's 2.0 line is a product decision the owner reconciles when the facade ships from this repository.
- `CHANGELOG.md` carries `## [0.1.0] - Unreleased` instead of `## [Unreleased]`, because `version --check` requires an entry for the workspace version before anything is released.
- The `milestone` concept of pamoja's front page is `goal` in xtask; the `web/home.toml` key is `[[goal]]`.
- `standards --check` stays red until the release 1 conformance tests exist; it is listed in CI's rust job, so the first CI run is red on that step by design.

### Foundation

- no_std to no_std dependencies are inline `{ path, version, default-features = false }` with a `std` forwarding feature rather than `workspace = true`, because Cargo ignores `default-features = false` on an inherited dependency.
- Publishable crates inherit `keywords` and `categories` from the workspace as well as the six named fields.
- zero-serve and xtask were created with `cargo new --bin`; zero-serve's binary is named `zero`.
- zero-ffi's `zero_version` carries `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` because `#[no_mangle]` counts as unsafe code under the lint.
- The bundle re-exports `zero-static` as `files`; each bundle feature enables the capabilities its crate is built over; the bundle excludes zero-ffi.
- No `.docker/lint-image.built` marker; the `std` feature comment says `impls`.

### xtask

- Modules dropped: hardware, prices, profiles, footprint, diagram, i18n, schema, examples, guides, buttons, theme, site/block.rs. catalog.rs and regions.rs were kept.
- lints.rs reads `[[crate]]` rows (name, lint, no_std) from docs/capabilities.toml; a no_std crate is held to the nostd table with its named table applied over it.
- `all = "warn"` became `all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }` in the root manifest, the three docs/lints tables, 19 member manifests and the two binding manifests, because clippy's `lint_groups_priority` fails otherwise.
- The audited `[lints]` table was appended to bindings/node and bindings/python/packages/native (which then broke both crates; fixed by the verifier as above).
- version.rs: PROSE_SITES = README.md and docs/about/releasing.md; PYTHON_PREFIX `zero-server`; ZERO_RELEASE_RETRY_SECS.
- builds.rs rows are zero-server feature sets; `packages` and `standards` have their own entry points; links.rs checks only the standards register.
- Site domain placeholder `zero-server.molex.cloud`; favicon `/assets/zero-icon.svg`; registry naming applied in catalog.rs and packages.rs.

### Policy

- bans.allow lists the 30 non-xtask workspace members and cbindgen's build-only graph; `[graph] exclude = ["xtask"]`.
- Nine `[[bans.features]]` overrides for default features inside cbindgen's tree; `skip-tree = cbindgen`; build.allow-build-scripts extended with the measured build scripts; the addenda restrict targets to the eleven aws-lc-sys targets.
- cargo vet ran in a container and rewrote supply-chain/config.toml, dropping the policy comment; no trust entry because rustls is not yet in the graph.
- justfile: docs-check runs only `cargo xtask docs --check`; `vet` and `deny-features` recipes added.

### Bindings

- rust-version 1.89 in both binding crates; pyo3-stub-gen behind a `stubs` feature; pyo3-async-runtimes and tokio omitted.
- NativeMethods.cs declares six exports ahead of the header (zero_last_error_message, zero_string_data, zero_string_free, zero_buffer_len, zero_buffer_data, zero_buffer_free) and ZeroStatus mirrors design 8.1; calling them before zero-ffi exports them throws EntryPointNotFoundException.
- `[assembly: DisableRuntimeMarshalling]` set; Authors molexxxx; PackageIcon conditional on the asset existing; smoke csproj copies conditional on existence.
- Homepage fields use https://z-server.dev; minimal guides and test.js added; generated artifacts committed as pamoja commits them; no .gitignore under bindings/dotnet; short README.md per package.

### Workflows

- actions/cache instead of Swatinem/rust-cache; msrv excludes zero-bench and zero-serve too; pypi-backfill's matrix expanded to the seven targets; issue templates rewritten for a server product; `conformance` label replaces `profile`; badges.yml takes zero-server's dispatch form; docs site host https://z-server.dev; miri skips zero-server-crypto; deny addendum invoked with `--manifest-path crates/zero-io/Cargo.toml --features io-compio`; pages.yml drops the dashboard steps; reproducible pins rust:1.89-bookworm by digest; musl NuGet rows use cargo zigbuild; NuGet/login user molexxxx.

### Docs

- api-surface.json holds 228 exports, not 238; canonical ids namespaced by scope; one `[[entry]]` per conformance statement (515 rows) with `release` and `current_release = 1`; the section 12.1 HTTP/3 rows are not yet fetched; release assignments listed in the agent's result; web/home.toml scenario groups are `server` and `bindings`; capabilities.toml adds `[[crate]]`, `[tooling]` and `[injects]`; SECURITY.md carries nine inventory sections; CONTRIBUTING's Docker recipe adds the memory and pid limits; scripts/lint-wording.mjs added; generated prose normalized to American spelling.

## Unverified

- `cargo xtask standards --check` cannot pass until the 123 release 1 rows have their cited tests; only `routing-01` was observed because the check stops at the first problem.
- `cargo xtask docs`, `packages`, `site` and `links` were not run end to end: the docs pages, the web tree and the binding package trees they render do not exist yet, so the eleven ignored xtask tests remain unexercised.
- The bare-metal `thumbv7em-none-eabihf` build: no rustup on this host; only the host `--no-default-features` checks ran.
- `rust-version = "1.89"`: exercised with cargo 1.96 locally and rustc 1.98.1 in the container; the MSRV CI job is what makes the number true. Whether xtask's oxc 0.150 and syn 3 build on 1.89 is unverified (pamoja excludes xtask from that job).
- `cargo publish --dry-run` and `cargo xtask release --dry-run` were not run; `--plan` needs no network and passed.
- The container syncs the stable channel (1.98.1) on every run because rust-toolchain.toml pins `stable`; fmt and clippy results are for that version.
- cargo deny, cargo vet and just were validated by the policy agent in a container on 2026-09-30 and were not rerun here; the xtask dependency graph is excluded from cargo-deny and covered by cargo vet exemptions.
- The .NET, Node and Python end-to-end smoke runs (dotnet run, node test.js, pytest) were done by the bindings agent on a debug build and were not repeated; only the two Rust binding crates were checked and linted here.
- No workflow has run; every crate name, feature name and path in .github/workflows depends on files that other agents own, and the Linux, macOS, musl and aarch64 builds have not been attempted on this host.
- The `## [0.1.0] - Unreleased` changelog heading was not checked against release-github.yml's notes extraction; the date must be set when the tag is cut.


## After the verifier (2026-09-30, owner session)

- Planning files moved into the repository: `.docs/DESIGN.md`, `.docs/ROADMAP.md` (R.8 added: the molexcloud-remake proof application), `.docs/research/` (nine notes plus the zero-server salvage map), `.docs/architectures/` (three proposals), `.docs/data/` (TechEmpower extractions, dependency-tree measurements). `.docs/` is gitignored; the copy in `zero-server/.myshit/ZERO-CORE-DESIGN.md` is a snapshot.
- Binding probe sources placed where `cargo xtask probes` expects them: `bench/probes/node/` (bench-probe.js and the napi-probe crate), `bench/probes/python/` (bench_probe.py and the pyo3-probe crate), `bench/probes/dotnet/` (pinvoke-bench and the ffi-probe crate). The Windows desktop results that section 8.6 of the design cites are kept beside them as `rerun-<lang>-windows.txt`. The three probe crates are listed in the workspace `exclude` so a cargo invocation inside them does not claim workspace membership; `cargo check --workspace` passes after the change. Build outputs that came with the copy (`probe.node`, `pyo3_probe.pyd`, the .NET `obj/` tree) were deleted; the repository `.gitignore` scopes `bin/` and `obj/` to `bindings/dotnet/`, so `bench/probes/dotnet/**/bin/` and `obj/` need a rule before anyone builds the probe on the host.
- `cargo xtask probes node` ran end to end (node:24 image, toolchain installed into the two named volumes, napi-probe built in the container) and wrote `bench/probes/rerun-node-linux.txt`. Linux container numbers against the Windows desktop numbers the design used: sync crossing 12.1 ns (Windows 12.0), External allocation 967 ns (918 to 826), threadsafe-function round trip 700 ns at 256 in flight (Windows 507 ns at 64 or more), batched 256 items per crossing 441 ns per item (Windows 125 ns), fire-and-forget 330 ns. The container is Docker Desktop's WSL2 virtual machine under a 3 GB memory cap and a 400 process cap, not bare-metal Linux, so the batched figure is a lower bound on what a Linux host does and the design's per-cell Node budget stays provisional until the harness host exists. Python and .NET reruns were started the same way; their result files are `rerun-python-linux.txt` and `rerun-dotnet-linux.txt` when present.
- The local rules file gained a "Currency" section (versions and dates fetched from registries and support pages, docs read at the pinned version, adoption checks before a crate enters `deny.toml`, failed fetches reported as unverified, dependency bumps as their own commits). The same rule set was added to the owner's global rules and, in shorter form, to the Node repository's local rules file.
- Python rerun (python:3.13 image, GIL build 3.13.15): callback with the thread attached once 37 ns (Windows 36), batched 256 items per call 21 ns per item (Windows 16), pyclass allocation 110 ns (Windows 196), attach per call 6,899 ns (Windows 2,219). The 150 ns Python budget of design section 8.6 holds in the container; the per-call attach cost is the figure the design already avoids by attaching once per batch.
- .NET probe: the first container run built ffi-probe, zero-ffi and the C# project but failed to load the native library because Program.cs still resolved pamoja's Windows DLL path from the research session; the resolver now loads zero_ffi and ffi_probe from the executable's directory with per-platform file names and the version benchmark calls zero_version. Result recorded below when the rerun completes.
- .NET rerun (mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 image, .NET 10.0.12 on Ubuntu 24.04): LibraryImport call 4.8 ns (Windows 4.5), with SuppressGCTransition 2.1 ns (Windows 3.0), reverse P/Invoke 3.9 ns (Windows 2.7), one-time thread attach 40,529 ns (Windows 11,100), view fill 1.2 ns (Windows 1.3), view fill plus UTF-8 decode of a 24-byte path 22.0 ns (Windows 18.0). The 25 ns .NET budget of design section 8.6 holds; the thread attach cost is the figure the design already pays once per managed thread, never per request.
- License: the owner created github.com/molexxxx/zero-core (public) with an Apache 2.0 LICENSE and chose Apache-2.0 only over the design's MIT. LICENSE-MIT and its nine package copies were replaced by LICENSE (GitHub's file, appendix left as published), the workspace and binding manifests, package.json files, pyproject classifiers, the .NET pack rule, the xtask package generator and site templates, README, CONTRIBUTING, the issue template and web/home.toml now say Apache-2.0; the site footer also lost pamoja's 'IoT, robotics, and drones' sentence. Design sections 3, 11 and 14 still say MIT and are superseded by this note.
- CI: the standards check in ci.yml runs with continue-on-error until the release 1 conformance tests exist; release-preflight.yml runs the same check as a blocking step before a tag publishes. The three probe crates under bench/probes are excluded from the workspace.
- The README no longer links the Node repository, which is archived after the 1.x support window; it names the product and the packages instead.
- First commit 4a578d9 'Scaffold the zero-core workspace' pushed to github.com/molexxxx/zero-core main on top of GitHub's initial commit (267 files; staged content checked for ignored paths and for any assistant, working-folder or session reference before the commit: none). CI outcome of this push is recorded in the owner's session notes, not here.

## First CI run (2026-09-30, commit 4a578d9) and the fixes

node and codeql were green; ci, python, dotnet and the Pages deploy were red, every failure on a step the verifier had listed as never exercised on this host. Each cause and change:

- python: the stub generator binary requires the `stubs` feature; the workflow now passes `--features stubs`.
- dotnet: the guides sample project pamoja ships did not exist; `bindings/dotnet/samples/ZeroServer.Guides` now holds the runner, the Guide helper and a version guide with the same anchors as the Node and Python guides, added to the solution, and runs locally against a release build of zero-ffi.
- ci, io-compio test run: zero-io declared no backend features; `io-tokio` (default) and `io-compio` now exist on zero-io and are forwarded by zero-http, zero-server and zero-bench. The compio backend itself is still unwritten (roadmap step 8).
- ci, hardened build: `-Clto` in RUSTFLAGS is refused for rlib targets; the job now uses linker-plugin LTO through clang and lld with rustc's own LTO off, per the sanitizer page of the unstable book (fetched).
- ci, cargo vet: CI installed cargo-vet 0.10.0 from GitHub releases while crates.io has 0.10.2, and the two serialize the store differently; `cargo vet fmt` with 0.10.2 left the store unchanged and `cargo vet --locked` passes (24 audited, 138 exempted), so the job now installs 0.10.2 from crates.io. cargo-deny is pinned to 0.20.2 the same way.
- ci, cargo deny: the binding graphs carry napi and PyO3 trees the root allowlist does not know, and both bindings declared zero-ffi by path without a version (a wildcard under the policy). `deny/node.toml` and `deny/python.toml` now hold each binding's full policy (the root file repeated plus the measured graph and its default-feature overrides), the workflow passes them with `--config`, and both manifests pin `version = "0.1.0"`. Both checks pass in the lint container on the committed file set; on the raw working tree the Node check also flags untracked build output under bindings/node, which a checkout never contains.
- docs check: `cargo xtask docs --check` requires a guide and a package per language for every capability before any exists; it is advisory (continue-on-error) in ci.yml and docs.yml while release 1 is built and blocking in release-preflight.yml, like the standards check. pages.yml runs on workflow_dispatch only until the documentation pages and the web tree exist.
- Not changed: the 14 Dependabot runs come from the copied dependabot.yml and will open version-bump pull requests on their schedule; the owner can thin the schedule if the volume is unwelcome.
- ci, hardened build, second round: the linker-plugin route fails on the runner because its lld (LLVM 18) cannot read bitcode from the nightly compiler (LLVM 23), and rustc requires -Clto with -Ccodegen-units=1 on every crate compiled under CFI while refusing -Clto for an invocation that emits an rlib beside a cdylib. The job now builds zero-ffi through cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib with both flags in RUSTFLAGS; validated in the lint container on nightly with -Zbuild-std (libzero_ffi.so links as DYN). Nightly cargo also warns that workspace.dependencies lists zero-ffi without a consumer and that zero-ffi depends on zero-http without using it yet; both are warnings on nightly only and are left for the step that wires zero-ffi to the HTTP driver.

## Repository rename (2026-09-30)

The owner chose one name for the product. On GitHub, molexxxx/zero-server (the Node SDK) became molexxxx/zero-server-node and molexxxx/zero-core became molexxxx/zero-server; the old name now resolves to this repository, so the Node repository's package.json, README badges, generators, types and docs site were repointed at zero-server-node in its working tree (uncommitted there) and its generated packages and docs rebuilt. In this tree every repository URL and every project-name mention moved to zero-server (the foundation crate keeps the crate name zero-core), the lint image is zero-server-lint (retagged locally), the probe volumes are zero-server-probe-cargo and zero-server-probe-rustup, and the README leads with the Rust workspace. Local folders are still projects/zero-server (Node) and projects/zero-core (Rust): the Node folder is the IDE workspace and the session's working directory, so the owner renames them with the IDE closed, zero-server to zero-server-node first, then zero-core to zero-server. The local rules file's Docker recipes use the current directory instead of a fixed path so the folder rename needs no edit.

CI on commit ee958bf: every job green (ci: fmt, clippy, test; bare-metal cross-compile; minimum supported rust; dependency audits; license and advisory audit; miri; sanitizers address and thread; fuzz smoke; reproducible build; hardened build checks; plus node, python, dotnet and codeql). The standards and docs checks run advisory until the release 1 tests and pages exist.
